This implies that Ezogabine may influence the metabolic activity of Ugt1a4 through its interaction with Nat2. The integration of these pathways highlights a possible mechanism where Ezogabine modulates the metabolic capacity of Ugt1a4, potentially affecting the body's ability to process certain compounds. The evidence suggests a dependency on Nat2, which in turn interacts with Ugt1a4, positioning Ezogabine as a regulator of Ugt1a4 activity. This relationship underscores the role of Nat2 as a bridge between Ezogabine and Ugt1a4, emphasizing the importance of intermediate proteins in mediating drug-target interactions.
